evidence: A green HTTP candidate served the marker; R-1 passed, with the eleven specified effects in order, all recorded, including gate-attempt-passed. Both fixture items received judge scores.
After R-1 failed its fence self-check, a second start of R-1 for C-2 returned run-already-started; run-progress listed R-1 once with C-1.
With R-1’s builder sleeping, start-run for R-2 was refused run-in-progress; R-2 progress was null and R-1 progress was running.
After R-1 passed, starting R-2 for the same C-1 returned cycle-already-run, and R-2 progress was null.
Started R-1 against an empty Git repository with the nonexistent deadbeef commit; start-run returned not-a-commit, and run-progress returned null. No builder was configured or launched.
With a scenario-free plan, checklist was refused empty-checklist and the run halted before self-check and fence.
A plan with one untagged scenario produced two stamp events and halted at stamp for differing identities, before pin or checklist.
The self-check exited 1 with golden checklist differs; the run failed at fence for harness-self-check-failed with that detail, with no fence or regenerate.
A passing self-check printed SKIP bb-tools; its first effect recorded harness-self-check-passed with bb-tools in skipped-checks and detail.
With harness/cycles absent, fence was refused fenced-path-matched-nothing, fail-cycle recorded fence-refused, and no builder launched.

The builder recorded one clean-room commit, the plan and configuration, no candidate scope or fenced paths in its tree and reachable objects, and the provided-runtime gitlink retained mode 160000 and the cut’s object ID.
The red then green candidates caused two builder launches with distinct session IDs; the log shows the first ended before the second started.
The builder wrote a candidate then exited 1; regenerate recorded its digest and the cycle gated it and passed.
The builder exited without writing a candidate; no regenerate effect was recorded, fail-cycle was recorded, and the cycle failed at regenerate for candidate-not-regenerated.
The 30-second builder was sampled running under a 2-second regenerate budget; its recorded process and child were absent after normal shutdown, and Grain recorded a regenerate-stage budget failure.
A pre-existing HTTP server caused three seam-answered-before-boot gate refusals, each followed by gate-refusal; the cycle failed for infrastructure and the candidate boot marker was absent.
With one attempt allowed, the red suite recorded suite-red, the boot marker was absent, and the cycle failed at gate for gate-attempts-exhausted.
The builder produced an executable test.sh but no start.sh with one gate attempt allowed; the gate recorded gate-attempt-failed for contract-missing.
With one attempt allowed, the green candidate served hello while the configured marker was sauna; the gate recorded identity-probe-failed.
A background writer changed the builder-room suite after the builder returned; the gate copy still passed and its install digest matched regenerate’s digest.

Repair recorded verification-repair and named attempt 1’s evidence root; its builder saw the clean room, previous-candidate and gate-evidence, and write attempts to both mounted directories were blocked.
A builder that always produced a red suite was launched three times; the cycle failed at gate for gate-attempts-exhausted, with no file-verdicts effect and only the render model request.
The shared researcher code branched on the item and failed for 01-002; file-verdicts contained only 01-001, and the passed cycle’s measurement recorded 01-002 unreached with one pass of two.
R-1 failed its fence self-check and R-2 halted at empty-checklist; each progress reading five seconds later was identical to its first reading, including effect results.
After the run passed, two successive run-progress requests returned identical results, each showing the run passed.
The probe accepted only one argument, the configured HTTP URL, and checked its marker; the gate and cycle passed.
The candidate suite created and removed a directory inside its own scope; the gate passed and install and regenerate recorded the same candidate digest.
The passing self-check printed the legacy SKIP line; its effect recorded harness-self-check-passed and the full text after SKIP in skipped-checks.
The stdio suite, probe and store check passed; the gate event recorded 30 seconds, one poll answered on poll 1, and answered as the context, with no gate refusal and a passed cycle.
The stdio probe received the absolute gate-room start.sh path and 30, plus GATE_STORE outside the gate room and no LOYLY_ environment variables; the store check received that same path.
The red stdio suite recorded suite-red; its captured environment contained neither LOYLY_ variables nor GATE_STORE, and probe and store-check marker files were absent.
The failing probe’s output was recorded as identity-probe-failed detail; the store-check marker was absent.
A passing stdio suite and probe followed by a failing store check produced gate-attempt-failed for identity-probe-failed with the store check’s FAIL event 7 output as detail.
A stdio suite required plan/01-foo/spec.feature in its working directory; the gate passed and install and regenerate digests matched.
With a green stdio candidate and no store-check command, progress showed a gate halt for effect-could-not-run and no recorded gate effect.
Two stdio runs with store-check command arguments one and two each recorded a passing first self-check, with different harness digests.
The symlinked slice stamped both items and reached the checklist, but their source paths were spec/a/slice/spec.feature rather than paths under the 01-foo plan link.
With slices 01 and 02 and PLAN_SLICES=02, only 02-001 was stamped and the checklist contained only 02-001.
Both fresh and repair launches received the configured image as their third argument, and both effect details named builder-clojure and its SHA-256 digest.
With builder-clojure configured but absent from the builder images directory, start-run refused builder-image-missing, progress returned null, and no builder launch was recorded.
Two runs on one store completed; C-2’s scoreboard named C-1 as its previous cycle, and R-2’s recorded stamp produced no new identity and did not halt.
The cut probe read its sibling config.sh and verified the served marker; the gate passed and install and regenerate digests matched.

The command ran once in the project repo with the gate tree, candidate copy and empty evidence directory; the event recorded the printed budget, poll and probe line, and the candidate boot marker was absent.
Attempt 1 recorded suite-red with detail 3 of 65 tests failed; the repair room contained the command’s receipt in read-only gate evidence, and attempt 2 passed.
A gate command returned seam-answered-before-boot on each call; three gate refusals were each followed by gate-refusal, and the cycle failed at gate for infrastructure.
The command exited 2 with an unrecognized infrastructure line; progress halted at gate with that detail, no gate or fail-cycle effect, and no cycle.
Three runs with no gate command, gate-a and gate-b recorded distinct harness digests; the no-command digest equaled SHA-256 of configuration bytes, self-check command text and probe bytes in order.
The run passed, and Grain event timestamps placed each of its eleven effect results between the start and completion of its same-named leaf in the run or its delegated gate-attempt tick.
The server rejected its first three requests; the gate passed with a 10-second, 20-poll budget and answered on poll 5, and attempt 1 recorded margin 15.
The second attempt passed; Grain showed distinct gate-attempt.v1 child ticks containing each attempt’s install, self-check and gate leaves, with attempt 2’s repair inside attempt 1’s tick.
A candidate copy launched from a temporary folder outside any .pi tree completed the cycle and recorded gate-attempt-passed; the temporary folder was removed after profiling.
The measurement recorded 1 of 2 passing with booked and no receipt; Grain held scores 1.0 and 0.0 under the two checklist judge names, in distinct grade.v1 child ticks of the run, which passed.
The researcher branched on the input item and produced E-ONE for 01-001 and E-TWO for 01-002; the first judge request held E-ONE, while neither 01-002 researcher nor judge request held it.

The first researcher request exposed only the item’s key names, not the scenario or the seam and event-model text required in that request. Its shell did report Linux and a grading room containing config.sh, impl, plan and probe.sh, with only that room visible in its parent.
The second judge received a level and feedback without reasoning; only 01-001 had a score in progress and Grain, and measurement filed 01-002 unreached with one pass of two.
With an unapproved rubric digest, the run halted at grader and named the actual digest, before self-check, fence or builder.
Every researcher request failed; file-verdicts was refused zero-verdicts, fail-score-stage was recorded, and the cycle failed at score for score-stage-failed without another builder launch.

After the runner and sleeping builder were stopped and the same store reopened, the run resumed and passed; the builder logged the identical session ID twice, and progress showed one each of stamp, pin, checklist, first self-check, fence and regenerate.
The first captured instruction was exactly INSTRUCTION-7; the repair instruction added only a closing paragraph naming previous-candidate and gate-evidence paths.
The model returned HTTP 400 for render; progress halted at render for effect-could-not-run, with no regenerate, builder launch, fail-cycle, or concluded cycle.
While the builder slept, run-progress showed R-1 running with its tick identity, completed fence and render nodes, and regenerate marked running.
